summary_ja: リスク・ファクターのモデル化可能性テストを四半期ごとに実施することと、内挿・外挿、期待ショート・フォールモデル、データ、ストレス期間、代理変数に関する要件を定める。
summary_en: Requires the risk factor modellability test quarterly and sets requirements for interpolation and extrapolation, the expected shortfall model, data, stress period risk factors and proxies.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall conduct the risk factor modellability test quarterly.

The risk factor modellability test shall satisfy all of the following requirements. (i) In classifying risk factors as modellable, only risk factors obtained by combinations of modellable risk factors are used, and the method prescribed in (a) or (b) below is used according to the category of case listed in (a) or (b). (a) Where interpolation by a combination of modellable risk factors (meaning calculating unobserved values lying between multiple observed, ordered data points; the same applies hereinafter in this (a)) is used: the interpolation is consistent with the interpolation method used in calculating the risk-theoretical profits and losses. In this case, when the number of risk factors is compressed while retaining as much information as possible, parameters may be derived from observations of modellable risk factors. (b) Where extrapolation by a combination of modellable risk factors (meaning calculating unobserved values lying outside multiple observed, ordered data points; the same applies hereinafter in this (b)) is used: the extrapolation is to be by a method of calculation using data of multiple modellable risk factors, and is consistent with the extrapolation method used in calculating the risk-theoretical profits and losses. In this case, when such extrapolation is used, the approval of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency shall be obtained in advance. (ii) The model that calculates expected shortfall (hereinafter in this Article and Article 253-6, paragraph (2), item (ii) referred to as the "expected shortfall model") captures general market risk and specific risk, and where it does not capture one or both of these risks, the market risk equivalent amount is calculated using non-modellable risk factors. (iii) The expected shortfall model takes into account the volatility and correlation coefficients of risk positions, and the data on that volatility and those correlation coefficients take into account the following matters. (a) Real price data is used. (b) Volatility is not underestimated. (c) Correlation coefficients are values that appropriately approximate correlations between real prices. (d) Where risk factors are transformed, volatility is not underestimated and the correlations arising from the risk factors used in the expected shortfall model are accurately reflected. (iv) The data used in the internal model approach satisfies all of the following requirements. (a) Where data not based on real prices is used, it is substantiated that the data substitutes for real prices. In this case, the consistency between that data and the price data used in the front office and the back office shall be confirmed. (b) Where a risk factor is derived from prices observed in the market, a document describing the method of derivation is prepared. (c) Business procedures for updating data sources are in place, and data is updated at a monthly frequency (or, where the data can be updated daily, at a daily frequency). (d) Where regression analysis is used to estimate the parameters of risk factors, the estimates of those parameters are regularly recalculated. (e) Calibration in valuation models (meaning estimating so that theoretical prices calculated from the expected shortfall model and other models relating to the calculation of the market risk equivalent amount fit as closely as possible the prices of actual transactions, including market prices) is performed with sufficient frequency. (f) Where missing values of risk factors are imputed, a clear policy is formulated. (v) The risk factors for expected shortfall assuming market turmoil prescribed in Article 254-3, paragraph (1) satisfy all of the following requirements. (a) Prices estimated from actual transaction prices or quotes are used. (b) Data covering as long a period as possible, including the business cycle, is obtained. (c) Where the nature of currently traded financial instruments differs from the nature of financial instruments traded during the stress period, it is substantiated, on the basis of historical data, that using the currently traded financial instruments is appropriate. (d) Where a currently traded financial instrument did not exist during the stress period, it is substantiated that the risk factor is broadly equivalent to the price or spread movements of similar financial instruments during the stress period, and all of the following requirements are satisfied. In this case, for a financial instrument whose nature has changed since the stress period, where it cannot be sufficiently explained that using current market data is appropriate, it shall be excluded from the risk factors for the stress period. (1) The requirement listed in Article 254-3, paragraph (2), item (i)(b) is satisfied. (2) Where, for the risk factor of a particular financial instrument relating to the calculation of expected shortfall, data on that financial instrument for the stress period is not available, the specific risk of that financial instrument's risk factor is not included in the reduced set of risk factors prescribed in Article 254-3, paragraph (1). (3) An exposure to a risk factor that is included in the risk factors of currently traded financial instruments and is not included in the reduced set of risk factors prescribed in Article 254-3, paragraph (1) is classified into the most appropriate risk factor included in that reduced set of risk factors. (vi) In using proxies, the region, type and other characteristics of the transactions in the financial instruments concerned are appropriately reflected, and the requirements prescribed in (a) or (b) below are satisfied according to the category of case listed in (a) or (b). (a) Where proxies are generated in a model based on multi-factors (meaning the elements relating to the region, type and other characteristics of transactions in financial instruments) (hereinafter in this (a) referred to as a "multi-factor model"): all of the following requirements are satisfied. (1) Where multiple indices are used in the multi-factor model, the correlations between the respective indices are captured. In this case, for the risk between indices that cannot be explained by the correlations, zero correlation is assumed. (2) The multi-factor model has significant explanatory power for asset price movements, and the existence of error that cannot be explained by the use of proxies is identified. (3) The coefficients of the multi-factor model are estimated on the basis of historical data. In this case, where those coefficients are set on the basis of subjective judgment, the risk factor shall be classified as a non-modellable risk factor. (b) Where proxies are used in the expected shortfall model: where the basis between the proxy and the risk factor is identified, that basis is appropriately classified into a modellable risk factor or a non-modellable risk factor, and the market risk equivalent amount is calculated, either of the following risk factors is reflected in the risk-theoretical profits and losses; provided, however, that where the classification has not been appropriately made, the risk factor of the proxy is reflected in the market risk equivalent amount and the risk-theoretical profits and losses. (1) The risk factor of the proxy and the risk factor of the basis. (2) A risk factor observed in the market.
